chapters.title: The Challenge
chapters.sourcePressure: The opening diagnosis is the gap between real capacity and the pattern of execution that ordinary weeks actually produce.
chapters.coreMove: Treat underperformance as an execution-pattern problem before looking for more ideas or inspiration.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the opening into generic motivation about reaching potential instead of a hard diagnosis of weak execution.

chapters.title: Redefining the Year
chapters.sourcePressure: Annualized thinking weakens urgency because a distant deadline lets focus leak until year-end pressure finally appears.
chapters.coreMove: Replace a distant annual horizon with a 12 week execution horizon that makes tradeoffs visible now.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating 12 weeks as a motivational trick or arbitrary productivity sprint rather than a pressure-producing execution frame.

chapters.title: The Emotional Connection
chapters.sourcePressure: New actions are often uncomfortable, so abstract importance loses unless the reader has a compelling emotional stake in the outcome.
chapters.coreMove: Tie the hard action to a felt future strong enough to beat comfort in the moment.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning vision into vague inspiration instead of an emotional lever for uncomfortable action.

chapters.title: Throw Out the Annual Plan
chapters.sourcePressure: The source rejects the annual plan as the execution frame and moves toward selective 12 week planning linked to goals.
chapters.coreMove: Cut a bloated annual plan down to the few 12 week goals and actions that can actually govern execution.
chapters.commonMisread: Hearing this as anti-planning, when the point is to reject the loose annual execution frame.

chapters.title: One Week at a Time
chapters.sourcePressure: A 12 week plan still needs a weekly bridge where priorities become current action inside real-week constraints.
chapters.coreMove: Translate the 12 week plan into a weekly set of actions that can survive the actual week in front of you.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing the chapter to making a to-do list instead of using the week as the operating unit of execution.

chapters.title: Confronting the Truth
chapters.sourcePressure: Execution needs measurable truth because intention alone hides whether the work is actually happening.
chapters.coreMove: Use visible measurement to replace intention with evidence about execution and results.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating truth as self-criticism instead of feedback that lets the system adjust.

chapters.title: Intentionality
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter shows that intention needs protection through yes/no decisions and blocked time.
chapters.coreMove: Turn intention into protected space by deciding what receives time and what must be refused.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating intentionality as having a positive attitude rather than protecting execution against competing demands.

chapters.title: Accountability as Ownership
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter redefines accountability as self-owned responsibility rather than surveillance, pressure, or punishment from others.
chapters.coreMove: Shift from waiting to be held accountable to owning the follow-through when conditions are imperfect.
chapters.commonMisread: Making accountability mean blame, shame, or another person monitoring compliance.

chapters.title: Interest versus Commitment
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter separates casual preference from durable commitment when comfort, convenience, or mood no longer cooperate.
chapters.coreMove: Test whether a goal is merely interesting or binding enough to command action when it becomes inconvenient.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating commitment as stronger enthusiasm instead of a different standard of follow-through.

chapters.title: Greatness in the Moment
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter moves commitment into present-tense performance on the next action in front of the reader.
chapters.coreMove: Shrink greatness from a distant identity into the quality of the action you choose in the current moment.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning greatness into grand ambition instead of present-tense execution.

chapters.title: Intentional Imbalance
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter argues for deliberate imbalance around priorities while preserving the limit against reckless neglect.
chapters.coreMove: Give disproportionate attention to the few actions that matter most, while naming what is being deferred and why.
chapters.commonMisread: Using imbalance as permission to neglect obligations permanently or selfishly.

chapters.title: The Execution System
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter consolidates principles, disciplines, the emotional cycle of change, and closed-loop execution into one coherent system.
chapters.coreMove: See execution as a closed system of recurring disciplines rather than isolated bursts of effort.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the system as a motivational checklist instead of a loop that keeps action, feedback, and adjustment connected.
mustNotDriftInto: new tactics not in the source

chapters.title: Establish Your Vision
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter builds the long-range vision that gives the 12 week cycle direction and emotional force.
chapters.coreMove: Draft a vision vivid enough to organize sacrifice and close enough to guide the next 12 week cycle.
chapters.commonMisread: Making vision a vague dream statement that has no power over tradeoffs or discomfort.

chapters.title: Develop Your 12 Week Plan
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter translates vision into a concrete 12 week plan with goals, structure, and written execution support.
chapters.coreMove: Convert vision into a written 12 week plan with few goals and concrete tactics that foster execution.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating plan writing as paperwork or as a wish list rather than the bridge from vision to action.

chapters.title: Installing Process Control
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter installs weekly routines and control mechanisms that keep the 12 week plan alive after it is written.
chapters.coreMove: Install a weekly operating routine that turns the plan into reviewed, scheduled, socially supported action.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking a written plan controls execution by itself, without weekly process control.

chapters.title: Keeping Score
chapters.sourcePressure: Scorekeeping makes progress visible, keeps execution honest, and changes behavior without becoming image management.
chapters.coreMove: Track execution visibly enough that the score tells you what to adjust before the cycle is over.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating scorekeeping as performance theater, self-worth, or elaborate metric design.

chapters.title: Take Back Control of Your Day
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter gives deliberate control over daily time so important work is protected from reactive demands.
chapters.coreMove: Design the day and week around protected performance time instead of letting reaction spend the calendar first.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating day control as calendar tidiness rather than protection for the work the score depends on.

chapters.title: Taking Ownership
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter turns ownership into concrete accountability actions that shrink excuse space inside the execution system.
chapters.coreMove: Create accountability through actions that claim agency before excuses can explain away the missed work.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning ownership into harsh self-talk or pretending every constraint is imaginary.
mustUseTerms: Actions to Create Greater Accountability in Your Life

chapters.title: 12 Week Commitments
chapters.sourcePressure: Commitments make priorities more binding after ownership, including personal commitments and commitments to others.
chapters.coreMove: Make the priority explicit enough that soft preference becomes a commitment with social and personal weight.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating commitment as ceremonial promise-making without concrete behavior and follow-up.

chapters.title: Your First 12 Weeks
chapters.sourcePressure: The first cycle carries predictable resistance: immediate gratification, old habits, victim thinking, multiple goals, and phase-specific pressure.
chapters.coreMove: Read first-cycle resistance as expected data, then adjust through the first, second, last four weeks and the 13th week review.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming early friction means the system failed or inventing magical week-by-week guarantees.

chapters.title: Final Thoughts and the 13th Week
chapters.sourcePressure: The closing chapter stays title-led: the 13th week should carry learning from one 12 week cycle into the next.
chapters.coreMove: Use the 13th week as a handoff from finish to review, reset, and recommitment.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the ending as emotional closure or celebration instead of the operating handoff into the next cycle.
